description: Bytebot is a self-hosted AI desktop agent that automates computer tasks through natural language commands, operating within a containerized Linux desktop environment.

summary.one_liner: Bytebot is a self-hosted AI desktop agent that runs in a containerized Ubuntu desktop and completes computer tasks from natural-language instructions.
summary.what_it_does: Bytebot gives an AI agent its own virtual Ubuntu Linux desktop (XFCE, Firefox, VS Code and other apps) where it can see the screen, move the mouse, type, and run programs. Users create tasks in a web UI by describing them in plain language, optionally uploading files such as PDFs for the agent to process. A live desktop view shows the work in progress, and a takeover mode lets a human step in. The agent is a NestJS service, the UI is Next.js, and it works with Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, and Google Gemini; the README also mentions LiteLLM for other providers such as Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, and Ollama. REST endpoints allow creating tasks and sending direct desktop actions like screenshots and clicks. Installed programs persist across tasks.
use_cases: automate multi-step computer tasks with natural language
download and organize files from websites
extract data from PDFs and spreadsheets
run AI-driven UI testing with screenshots
self-hosted alternative to browser-only AI agents
programmatic desktop control via REST API
how_to_run: git clone the bytebot repository and cd into it
echo your AI provider key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, or GEMINI_API_KEY) into docker/.env
Open the web UI in your browser to create tasks
Optional: deploy on Kubernetes with helm install bytebot ./helm --set agent.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...
notable: Agent has its own full virtual Linux desktop rather than only a browser
Takeover mode lets a human take control of the desktop
Installed programs and password managers persist for future tasks
Supports Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini, plus other providers via LiteLLM
Deployable with Docker Compose, Railway, or Helm on Kubernetes
caveats: Requires an API key from an AI provider; the agent uses paid model calls
Setup involves Docker or Kubernetes; the README gives no native install path
README does not describe resource requirements or security isolation details
keywords: extract data from pdf with ai
run ai on its own computer
